issuer: the Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles
note: The Vermont Statutes Online (read 2026-10-30): 23 V.S.A. § 608 charges $62 for a four-year operator's licence ($39 for two years); § 601 has it expire on the second or fourth anniversary of the birth date after issue; § 4 makes a junior operator anyone 16 or 17, so a (full) operator's licence is held from 18. § 115 issues a nondriver identification card to a resident without a licence for $29, expiring on the fourth anniversary of the birth date (4 years); no age is held for it.

sources.title: 23 V.S.A. § 608, Fees
sources.said: The four-year fee required to be paid the Commissioner for licensing an operator of motor vehicles or for issuing an operator’s privilege card shall be $62.00.

sources.title: 23 V.S.A. § 601, License required
sources.said: All operator’s licenses issued under this chapter shall expire, unless earlier cancelled, at midnight on the eve of the second or fourth anniversary of the date of birth of the license holder following the date of issue.

sources.title: 23 V.S.A. § 4, Definitions
sources.said: (16) “Junior operator” shall include only such persons as are 16 and 17 years of age.

sources.title: 23 V.S.A. § 115, Nondriver identification cards
sources.said: The Commissioner shall require payment of a fee of $29.00 at the time application for an identification card is made ... Every identification card shall expire, unless earlier canceled, at 12:00 midnight on the eve of the fourth anniversary of the date of birth of the cardholder following the date of original issue
